A1.justification: Both complete 22-page PDFs describe NeuroLM, with matching main sections and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on six EEG datasets in Tables 2–4, alongside ablations, training curves and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original six-dataset evaluations and the experimental analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The text-aligned neural tokenizer, multi-channel autoregressive pre-training and multi-task instruction tuning are unchanged, including their architectures and objectives in Section 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pre-training datasets and six downstream tasks. The HMC revision concerns subject counts and partitions within retained sleep-stage coverage, rather than a new dataset or population.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain SPaRCNet, ContraWR, CNN-Transformer, FFCL, ST-Transformer, BIOT and LaBraM-Base. Comparator membership in the supplementary analyses is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes HMC from 154 subjects, partitioned as subjects 1–100, 101–126 and 127–154, to 151 subjects partitioned into the first 100, middle 25 and last 26. This revises the reported split from 100/26/28 to 100/25/26. Neither PDF establishes whether experiments were rerun; other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The option-shuffling, instruction-data-size and autoregressive-pre-training ablations remain unchanged. Appendices E–G retain the same attention, tokenizer, embedding-alignment and pre-training-epoch analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three random seeds in Section 3.2. Uncertainty reporting in the tables and figures is unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported outcome values, plotted results and qualitative findings are retained. Despite the revised HMC split description, its numerical results are unchanged; for example, Table 3 reports NeuroLM-B balanced accuracy of 0.6737 ± 0.0050 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and Equations 1–8 are unchanged, including the variational interpretation and ELBO derivation in Section 2.2. No formal assumptions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about integrating EEG with language models, unified multi-task instruction tuning, approximately 25,000 hours of pre-training and evaluation across six datasets.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model scaling, HMC overfitting, TUSL data scarcity and comparison fairness are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same limitations concerning single-task performance, hyperparameter sensitivity and coarse EEG–text alignment.

D1.justification: The HMC partition documentation replaces explicit subject-number ranges with ordered groups of 100/25/26 subjects, revising the instructions for reproducing that split. Preprocessing, hardware, hyperparameters, instruction templates and code-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference entries are unchanged after matching them across page breaks. The introduction and Appendix A retain the same related-work discussion and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds an Acknowledgments section before the references, locally rewrites the HMC split passage and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining narrative and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgments shift the reference heading and redistribute bibliography entries across pages 11–14. All eleven figures and twelve tables retain their displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: The new acknowledgments disclose previously unreported funding, providing a modest transparency improvement. Methods, results, theory and limitations remain unchanged. The HMC count/split revision cannot independently establish improved experimental quality because the PDFs do not explain whether it corrects documentation or reflects rerun experiments.
